questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) I have been / (B) living in Mumbai / (C) since ten years. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'since' is used with a point in time (e.g., since 2015). With a DURATION use 'for'. Correct: '…for ten years'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) The committee / (B) have decided / (C) to postpone the meeting. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'Committee' is a collective noun acting as a single unit here (unanimous decision) → singular verb 'has decided'. 'Have' would be right only if the members were acting individually or disagreeing.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) The number of candidates / (B) applying for the post / (C) are increasing every year. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a SINGULAR verb. Correct: 'is increasing'. Contrast: 'A number of candidates ARE applying' (plural). The difference is a classic examiner favourite.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) Neither the captain / (B) nor the players / (C) was present at the ceremony. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the SECOND (closer) subject. 'Players' is plural → verb should be 'were'. Correct: 'were present'. Subtle parallelism trap.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) Hardly had he left the office / (B) than the phone / (C) began to ring loudly. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: Fixed correlative pair: 'Hardly/Scarcely … WHEN'. Only 'No sooner' takes 'than'. Correct: '…hardly had he left the office WHEN the phone…'. Examiners swap these two constructions routinely.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) She said me / (B) that she would come / (C) to the party tomorrow. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'Said' does NOT take an indirect object directly. Correct: 'She TOLD me' or 'She said TO me'. The verb 'tell' takes the indirect object without a preposition; 'say' requires 'to'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) Each of the participants / (B) were given a certificate / (C) at the end of the workshop. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: Subject 'Each' (singular) takes a singular verb, regardless of the plural noun that follows. Correct: 'was given'. Trap: the plural 'participants' distracts from the real subject.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Identify the error: (A) One of my friends / (B) who live in Delhi / (C) have invited me to visit this month. / (D) No error
questions.explanation: 'One' is the subject of the main clause; the verb must be singular: 'has invited'. The relative clause 'who live in Delhi' modifies 'friends' (plural 'live' is correct THERE), but the main verb (C) must agree with 'One'.
questions.subject: English
